before.title: CVT Shudder Under Light Acceleration
before.description: The Jatco CVT paired with the VC-Turbo engine can develop a noticeable shudder during light acceleration from a stop. The CVT belt and pulleys exhibit inconsistent clamping force at low vehicle speeds.
before.solution: Perform a CVT fluid drain and refill with genuine Nissan NS-3 CVT fluid. A TCM recalibration at the dealer may resolve the issue. Severe cases may require valve body replacement.

before.description: The QX50 InTouch infotainment system suffers from slow response times, frequent Bluetooth disconnections, and occasional screen blackouts. The dual-screen setup amplifies the frustration when both displays become unresponsive.
before.solution: Update to the latest firmware via USB download from Infiniti. Perform a system reset by holding the power button. Clear paired Bluetooth devices and re-pair to resolve connectivity issues.

before.title: Premature Front Lower Control Arm / Compression Rod Bushing Wear Causing Clunks and Tire Wear
before.description: The FM-platform suspension used under the QX50 is known for front lower control arm and compression rod bushing wear, especially on rough roads or vehicles with larger wheel packages. Owners report clunking over bumps, vague steering, braking shimmy, and uneven front tire wear. Once the fluid-filled bushings crack or leak, alignment stability suffers and the vehicle can feel unsettled during braking or lane changes.
before.solution: Inspect front lower control arm bushings, compression rod bushings, ball joints, and sway bar links with the suspension loaded. Replace worn arms or bushings in pairs, then perform a four-wheel alignment and inspect tires for cupping or inner-edge wear. Many owners choose complete arm assemblies to reduce labor and avoid pressing bushings.

communityRecommendations.content: Replace worn suspension arms in pairs and align the vehicle immediately afterward; replacing only one side often leaves the steering feel inconsistent.
If you have repeated inner-edge tire wear, ask the shop to inspect compliance bushings and toe settings, not just the tires.
Aftermarket complete control arm assemblies are popular because they include new bushings and ball joints, reducing labor compared with pressing bushings.
Sway bar end links are often replaced at the same time if clunks persist after control arm work.

before.title: Steering Wheel Lock / Ignition No-Start from Electronic Steering Lock Failure
before.description: Infiniti/Nissan vehicles using the electronic steering column lock system have a well-documented failure mode where the vehicle will not recognize the lock state, leaving the car unable to start even though the battery and key fob appear normal. The issue is widely discussed across Nissan/Infiniti owner communities and tied to the steering lock control unit used on related FM-platform vehicles. Owners typically report a sudden no-start with the steering wheel locked or the ignition staying in ACC/ON behavior without cranking.
before.solution: Confirm battery voltage and key fob operation first, then scan BCM/IPDM/steering lock modules for communication or lock-status faults. Repair usually involves replacing or bypassing the failed electronic steering lock assembly depending on model applicability and local repair practice, followed by key/immobilizer relearn if required. Because symptoms mimic a weak battery or bad brake switch, proper diagnosis is important before replacing parts.
symptoms: vehicle stuck in ACC or ON mode

citations.title: NHTSA Complaint Database - Infiniti QX50 no-start / steering lock related complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Before condemning the steering lock, verify the 12V battery is fully charged and load-tested; low voltage can trigger misleading intelligent-key and lock errors.
If the vehicle intermittently fails to start, scan BCM and immobilizer modules immediately while the fault is active; stored history can disappear after battery disconnects.
A strong AGM battery helps prevent low-voltage false immobilizer and steering lock symptoms that often confuse diagnosis.
Owners and independent shops often use a memory saver during battery replacement or electrical diagnosis to reduce relearn hassles on push-button-start Infiniti models.

before.title: Sunroof Drain / HVAC Evaporator Water Intrusion Causing Wet Carpets and Electrical Faults
before.description: A recurring complaint on Infiniti crossovers and sedans of this era is water entering the cabin from clogged or poorly routed sunroof drains, and in some cases from HVAC evaporator drain issues. QX50 owners report soaked front footwells, musty odor, fogging windows, and intermittent electrical problems when water reaches connectors or modules under the dash or carpet. Left unresolved, the issue can damage harnesses, audio components, and interior trim while promoting mold growth.
before.solution: Inspect all four sunroof drains, drain grommets, A-pillar routing, and the HVAC evaporator drain for blockage or disconnection. Clear drains with low-pressure air or line, repair cracked hoses, and dry the carpet and underlayment thoroughly; if water reached connectors, inspect for corrosion and repair affected wiring. Many owners also modify or extend drain outlets to reduce repeat clogging.
symptoms: intermittent electrical glitches after rain or car wash

citations.title: NHTSA Vehicle Complaints - 2017 Infiniti QX50 (water leak / visibility / electrical owner complaints)

communityRecommendations.content: Do not use high-pressure compressed air directly into the drain tubes; it can separate old hoses behind trim and make the leak worse.
After fixing the leak, pull up the carpet and dry the padding completely with fans or a dehumidifier, otherwise odor and corrosion often return.
Flexible trimmer line is commonly used by owners to clear sunroof drains without puncturing the hose.
Electrical contact cleaner helps restore connectors exposed to moisture after the source of the leak is repaired.

before.title: Timing Chain / VVEL Rattle and Front Timing Cover Oil Leaks on VQ37VHR
before.description: Owners of the 3.7L VQ37VHR-equipped QX50 report a metallic rattle at cold start and oil seepage from the front timing cover area. On this engine, timing chain guide/tensioner wear and RTV-sealed front cover leaks can develop with age and heat cycling; because the VVEL/timing components sit behind the front cover, diagnosis often starts with distinguishing harmless brief startup noise from persistent chain or guide wear. Multiple owner complaints and repair discussions note oil smell, visible seepage down the front of the engine, and expensive labor because the front cover must be resealed and timing components inspected at the same time.
before.solution: Inspect for oil seepage around the front timing cover, upper oil pan junction, and valve cover areas to confirm the leak source before authorizing repairs. If startup rattle is persistent or worsens, check chain tensioner operation and timing correlation, then reseal the front cover with OEM-equivalent RTV and replace worn guides/tensioners as needed. Because labor overlap is substantial, many owners replace the water pump, drive belt, and related seals during the same job.
symptoms: metallic rattle for 1-3 seconds on cold start
oil seepage on front of engine
small oil spots under front of vehicle

citations.title: NHTSA Vehicle Complaints - 2016 Infiniti QX50 (engine/oil leak related owner complaints)

communityRecommendations.content: Have the leak source dye-tested first; valve cover seepage can mimic a front cover leak, and misdiagnosis can turn a moderate repair into a very expensive one.
If the front cover is being removed, ask the shop to inspect timing chain guides, tensioners, and water pump at the same time to avoid duplicate labor later.
Owners commonly use OEM-style RTV when resealing Nissan/Infiniti timing covers because improper sealant choice is a common cause of repeat leaks.
communityRecommendations.partName: Ultra Grey RTV Silicone Gasket Maker

communityRecommendations.content: A fresh belt is often installed during front-engine service since it must be removed anyway and heat/oil contamination shortens belt life.

before.title: VC-Turbo Engine Oil Consumption
before.description: The variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) KR20DDET engine in the QX50 is known for higher-than-normal oil consumption, sometimes requiring top-offs between scheduled oil changes. The complex variable compression mechanism adds more internal surfaces where oil can be consumed.
before.solution: Monitor oil levels every 1,000 miles and top off as needed. Use only 0W-20 full synthetic oil meeting Nissan specifications. Infiniti has extended the powertrain warranty on some VINs to address this concern.
symptoms: Low oil level warning between changes
Oil consumption exceeding 1 qt per 3,000 miles
